summary: Phones attach any file, as the desktop composer does. The phone uploads the bytes over app:upload-attachment ({ name, data } in base64, 10 MB at most so one message fits the OkHttp 16 MiB send queue and the IAP 32 MiB line); the backend saves them under <data dir>/attachments/<uuid>/<name> and answers the path. The turn is the desktop's shape (attachmentTurn): the provider text ends with one [Attached file "x" is saved at: /path] line per file, the display body with a [[pill:id]] token drawn as a file chip. A backend without attachment_upload_v1 takes images only. The backend image shrink also turns a JPEG upright from its EXIF orientation before it drops the EXIF, and the headless server prunes copies older than 30 days at start.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: The Expo composer gains file attach, refusals and the large-paste chip; until then it sends images only, as before

storageDataMigration.reason: An uploaded file is saved in the same attachments folder as a desktop attachment, and a sent one is an ordinary file pill in pills_meta. On Android a draft or queued file is an ordinary attachment row whose path column holds the saved file as JSON under its own MIME type; no table or column changes.
